results.question: Show me week-over-week signup trends for startup-type users only, broken down by revenue range, for the last 3 months.
results.answer: Startup signups show a sharp acceleration starting mid-January, with pre-revenue companies driving the surge — jumping from 33 signups (12 Jan-18 Jan) to 105 (19 Jan-25 Jan), then 136 (26 Jan-1 Feb), and peaking at 209 (2 Feb-8 Feb). The above-5-crore segment follows a similar but smaller spike, rising from 3 to 14 signups between 12 Jan and 25 Jan before settling to single digits in February. Earlier weeks (late September through December) show minimal activity across all revenue ranges, typically 1-3 signups per week, making the late-January pre-revenue surge the standout pattern in this three-month window; note that appears across 13 distinct weeks in the full dataset (per the group counts), 1-5-crore across 16, and above-5-crore across 12.
results.sql_used: SELECT week_range, company_revenue_range, cnt FROM (SELECT week_range, COALESCE(company_revenue_range, 'unknown') AS company_revenue_range, year_monthnumber_weekstart_order AS wk, COUNT(DISTINCT userid) AS cnt FROM nep_liftoffx_data_sample WHERE activity_type = 'signup' AND company_type = 'startup' GROUP BY week_range, COALESCE(company_revenue_range, 'unknown'), year_monthnumber_weekstart_order ORDER BY wk DESC LIMIT 100) s ORDER BY wk, company_revenue_range LIMIT 500

results.question: Compare signup counts for startups vs MSMEs, filtered to only pre-revenue and 1-5 crore revenue ranges, grouped by signup month.
results.answer: Startup signups outpace MSMEs consistently across all months, with the gap widening dramatically over time: from a modest 3 vs 2 in October 2025 to a substantial 690 vs 262 in February 2026. The most notable jump occurs between December 2025 (5 startup signups, no MSME data recorded) and January 2026, where both categories surge sharply — startups to 364 and MSMEs to 203 — suggesting a major inflection point in adoption for pre-revenue and 1-5 crore revenue companies. By February 2026, startups reach 690 signups, more than double the MSME count of 262, reinforcing startups as the dominant segment in this filtered view.
results.sql_used: SELECT SUBSTRING(created_datetime::text, 1, 7) AS signup_month, company_type, COUNT(*) AS signups FROM nep_master_user_table_sample_data WHERE company_type IN ('startup', 'msme') AND company_revenue_range IN ('pre-revenue', '1-5-crore') GROUP BY SUBSTRING(created_datetime::text, 1, 7), company_type ORDER BY signup_month, company_type LIMIT 500

results.question: Show me the top 10 AI conversation queries asked by MSME users who signed up after January 2026, along with their response flow state.
results.answer: "How do I grow my business faster?" leads with 7 asks from 7 distinct users, followed by "How can I find new customers and expand my market?" at 3 asks/3 users — both signaling straightforward growth-oriented intent among MSME users. The AI-audience-research prompt template appears in three variants (a blank placeholder version asked 5 times by 4 users, plus two "Refurbished Plastic Bags / North India" variants asked once each), suggesting users are reusing and lightly editing a shared prompt template rather than writing original queries. results.question: Compare the average number of weekly activities between Internal Users and External Users, further segmented by MSME vs startup.
results.answer: External Users significantly outpace Internal Users in weekly activity volume, with External-startup users averaging 1,364.36 activities per week (11 active weeks, 15,008 total) and External-msme averaging 1,235.0 (7 active weeks, 8,645 total) — both far higher than either internal segment. Among Internal Users, startups also show notably stronger engagement than msme (543.14 vs 191.45 weekly average, despite both tracking 22 active weeks), suggesting startup-affiliated users are consistently more active regardless of internal or external status. The standout anomaly is External-msme's low week count (7) compared to the other three segments (11 and 22), meaning its high average of 1,235.0 is drawn from a much shorter observation window.
results.sql_used: SELECT s.user_type || ' - ' || s.company_type AS segment, s.user_type, s.company_type, ROUND(AVG(s.activity_count), 2) AS avg_weekly_activities, COUNT(*) AS weeks_with_activity, SUM(s.activity_count) AS total_activities FROM (SELECT l.user_type AS user_type, l.company_type AS company_type, l.week_range AS week_range, COUNT(*) AS activity_count FROM nep_liftoffx_data_sample l WHERE l.user_type IN ('Internal Users', 'External Users') AND l.company_type IN ('msme', 'startup') GROUP BY l.user_type, l.company_type, l.week_range) s GROUP BY s.user_type, s.company_type ORDER BY s.user_type, s.company_type LIMIT 500

results.question: How many users who signed up in October 2025 were still active in February 2026, broken down by company type and revenue range?
results.answer: The overwhelming majority of October 2025 signups (894 out of 900 total) fall into an unclassified company type/revenue segment, yet only 34 of these retained through February 2026 — a stark 3.8% retention rate that drags down overall performance. In contrast, the small cohort of classified accounts (6 users across startup and msme segments) shows near-perfect retention, with 5 of 6 still active, including 100% retention for startups in the 1-5-crore and pre-revenue ranges and msme accounts in above-5-crore and pre-revenue ranges. The lone exception is a single msme user in the 1-5-crore range who did not remain active, resulting in 0% retention for that specific segment.
results.sql_used: SELECT u.company_type, u.company_revenue_range, COUNT(DISTINCT u.user_id) AS signed_up_oct_2025, COUNT(DISTINCT act.userid) AS still_active_feb_2026, ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT act.userid)::NUMERIC / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT u.user_id), 0) * 100, 2) AS retention_pct FROM nep_master_user_table_sample_data u LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT userid FROM nep_liftoffx_data_sample WHERE created_at >= '2026-02-01' AND created_at < '2026-03-01') act ON act.userid = u.user_id WHERE u.created_datetime >= '2025-10-01' AND u.created_datetime < '2025-11-01' GROUP BY u.company_type, u.company_revenue_range ORDER BY still_active_feb_2026 DESC LIMIT 500

Engagement drops off steeply after the top events, with mid-tier actions like profile_dropdown_opened (110) and profile_change_language_clicked (84) showing this one user interacting heavily with navigation and settings before tapering into lower-frequency actions like thumbs_up_clicked (10) and Clicked on Mic (6).

results.answer: Out of 87 EXPERT-type mentors across these two states, Karnataka leads with 49 mentors versus Maharashtra's 38, and Bangalore alone accounts for 47 of those Karnataka entries (with just 1 each in Krishnarajasagara and Sarjapur). results.question: For each program, show the count of active mentors broken down by country and venture stage expertise.

results.question: Compare the industry coverage of mentors in Liftoff-Spark vs Liftoff-Propel, filtered to only ACTIVE mentors with PUBLIC visibility in India.
results.answer: Both programs cover 49 industries each among active, public-visibility mentors in India, indicating equally broad industry diversification. Software and IT Services leads both programs but with Spark slightly ahead (24 vs 22 mentors), and this pattern of Spark having marginally higher headcounts repeats across most shared categories — Education and Training (20 vs 17), Fintech (20 vs 17), and Agritech and Food Processing (10 vs 7). One naming inconsistency worth flagging: Propel lists "Pharmaceuticals, Healthcare and Wellness" (7) and "Pharmaceuticals Healthcare and Wellness" (6) as separate entries, and Spark shows the same split (7 and 8), suggesting a punctuation-based duplicate category that's fragmenting what should likely be a single industry group in both programs.

results.sql_used: SELECT 'event_gap_area' AS category, gapkey AS label, COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) AS cnt FROM nep_master_live_events_data WHERE program_key IN ('liftoff-spark', 'liftoff-propel') AND gapkey IS NOT NULL GROUP BY gapkey UNION ALL SELECT 'mentor_industry' AS category, industry_name AS label, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS cnt FROM nep_mentor_profiles_sample_data WHERE program IN ('liftoff-spark', 'liftoff-propel') AND industry_name IS NOT NULL GROUP BY industry_name LIMIT 500

results.question: For pre-revenue users, compare signup-to-first-activity conversion time between traffic sources.

results.question: Compare time between signup and first AI message for users from different revenue ranges.
results.answer: Pre-revenue companies show the fastest engagement, with users sending their first AI message just 4.7 days after signup on average, compared to 5.2 days for above-5-crore companies and 5.7 days for 1-5-crore companies. The pattern isn't strictly linear with revenue size—1-5-crore users are actually slower to engage (5.7 days) than the larger above-5-crore segment (5.2 days), despite representing a mid-tier revenue bracket. With sample sizes of 23-31 users per group, the overall spread between fastest and slowest cohorts is exactly 1 day, suggesting revenue range has a modest but real effect on onboarding speed.
results.sql_used:
SELECT
  a.company_revenue_range,
  COUNT(DISTINCT a.userid) AS users,
  ROUND(AVG(fm.first_msg - a.signup_date)::NUMERIC, 1) AS avg_days_to_first_message
FROM nep_liftoffx_data_sample a
JOIN (
  SELECT userid, MIN(message_date) AS first_msg
  FROM nep_liftoffx_data_sample
  WHERE activity_type = 'message'
    AND message_query IS NOT NULL
    AND message_date IS NOT NULL
    AND message_date > signup_date
  GROUP BY userid
) fm ON a.userid = fm.userid
WHERE a.activity_type = 'signup'
  AND a.company_revenue_range IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY a.company_revenue_range
ORDER BY avg_days_to_first_message
LIMIT 500

results.question: Show month-over-month event attendance trends, broken down by session type and program, for Dec 2025 to Jan 2026.
results.answer: Attendance rates improved sharply from December 2025 to January 2026 across all programs, with expertSession attendance jumping from roughly 4% (liftoff-propel and liftoff-spark, 2 of 49 registrants attended) to over 21-26% in January — liftoff-propel and liftoff-spark both hit 25.71% (9 of 35 attended), while liftoff reached 21.95% (9 of 41). SELECT
  TO_CHAR(start_date, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    program_key,
  sessiontype,
  COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) AS total_events,

results.sql_used: SELECT u.traffic_source_source AS traffic_source, COUNT(DISTINCT u.user_id) AS signups, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN u.profile_status = 'completedprofile' THEN u.user_id END) AS profile_completions, COUNT(DISTINCT msg.userid) AS first_ai_message, COUNT(DISTINCT reg.participant_user_id) AS first_event_registration, COUNT(DISTINCT att.participant_user_id) AS first_event_attendance FROM nep_master_user_table_sample_data u LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT l.userid FROM nep_liftoffx_data_sample l WHERE l.activity_type = 'message' AND l.message_query IS NOT NULL) msg ON msg.userid = u.user_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT e.participant_user_id FROM nep_master_live_events_data e) reg ON reg.participant_user_id = u.user_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT e2.participant_user_id FROM nep_master_live_events_data e2 WHERE e2.participant_status = 'ATTENDED') att ON att.participant_user_id = u.user_id WHERE u.user_type = 'External Users' AND u.company_type = 'startup' AND u.company_revenue_range = 'pre-revenue' GROUP BY u.traffic_source_source ORDER BY signups DESC LIMIT 500
